PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 1.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: EXT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS - DAY

lines.text: Pull off the forboding building and fly out over the trees...
It’s been 76 days, 2 hours and 37 minutes
since Young Ned’s father deposited him at the
Longborough School for Boys. And this, Young
Ned felt, was long enough.
Boy and Dog walk together...
He is a gifted boy, able to bring dead things
back to life with the touch of his finger.
Tired of the dark and joyless boarding school,
Young Ned and his dog, Digby, set out in
search of a new beginning.
Young Ned stops to open and sip from his belt-canteen and to
scratch Digby with his walking stick...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Alone in the forest, they didn’t know what to
expect. And least of all, they expected...
Ned looks ahead, perplexed...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...giant butterflies.
NED’S POV - EIGHT SIX-YEAR-OLD KIDS wearing big BUTTERFLY WINGS
surround a tree. Their young TEACHER, MS. MOSS, stretches to
reach a NEST on a branch just out of reach.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Ms. Moss believed every child was a butterfly
at heart, and her kindergartners knew that
“every caterpillar learns to fly.” To ensure
this fact was not forgotten, uniforms were
required, as well as frequent nature walks.
Young Ned sets down his kerchief/satchel, walks to the tree and
climbs up...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
On this day, Ms. Moss found herself just out
of reach of an important lesson on the life
cycle of the Yellow Canary.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
Young Ned stretches to reach the--
ANGLE - THE NEST - Resting on the branch. Young Ned leans into
frame, sees that the THREE BABY BIRDS are dead.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The Yellow Canaries, however, believed a
better lesson might have been the risks of
environmental toxins.
YOUNG NED - Looks back down at the smiling butterfly children.
He puts his finger into the nest and as we see the TINY SPARK...
BASE OF A TREE - MOMENTS LATER
Young Ned carries down the nest, NOW with three LIVE baby birds,
CHIRPING. The kids surround him excitedly to see...
In that moment, amidst beating wings and
smiling faces, Young Ned decided that new
beginnings were a wonderful thing.
Would you like to see our latest class project?
Ms. Moss REVEALS a large, covered cage. Ned reacts, uneasy.
And then he wasn’t so sure...
We’ve been nursing some Red-Breasted
Woodpecker chicks back to health, and today
we’re setting them free.
As the once-dead Yellow Canaries had now been
alive-again for over a minute, Young Ned knew
that by the rules of his gift, something else
nearby had to die.
Ms. Moss approaches the covered cage, as the children follow and
gather ‘round. Young Ned watches, growing nervous, starting to
back quietly away...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Unaware of the class project, the boy had thought
that whatever creatures traded their lives would
be small, random and hidden in the woods.
ANGLE from behind the cage--
As the children look on in anticipation as Ms. Moss prepares to
remove the small blanket that covers it...
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Sadly, this was not the case...
She pulls off the blanket. As the kids’ eyes go wide with shock--

scenes.heading: EXT. NORTH THRUSH COUNTRY ROAD - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: Young Ned, not looking pleased, and Digby walk back the way they
came. We HEAR the distant sound of kids yelling and crying...
As the boy and his dog returned from whence
they came, Young Ned concluded that new
beginnings only lead to painful ends.

scenes.heading: EXT. LIBERTY APARTMENT BUILDING - PRESENT DAY

lines.text: Establishing...
It’s 20 years later...

scenes.heading: INT. NED’S APARTMENT - NED’S BEDROOM - DAY

lines.text: Morning sunshine. Digby sleeps on the floor.
...and the boy has become a Pie-Maker, who is
in love.
We FIND NED, the grown-up version, lying in bed, eyes open...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It’s been 1 year, 22 weeks and 4 days since he
touched his childhood sweetheart and brought
her back to life.
He looks over and we REVEAL CHUCK’S EMPTY BED.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And 2 days, 10 hours and 28 minutes since
living-dead-girl Charlotte “Chuck” Charles
moved across the hall.
He lies back down, staring at the ceiling.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Whilst Chuck had called it “apartment-
sitting,” the Pie-Maker sensed a new beginning
beginning.

scenes.heading: INT. LIBERTY APARTMENT BUILDING - HALLWAY - DAY (TO BE SHOT)

lines.text: Both doors open and CHUCK and Ned step out at the same time.
Ned ready for work; Chuck in her kerchief and sunglasses.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED:
Morning. Sleep okay over there?
I woke up to the smell of someone cooking toast
and eggs. It blew in through my sun-dappled
curtains and I thought how lucky I am to be
alive in a world with sun-dappled anything. I
got so excited I was afraid my smile was going
to vibrate the veneer off the cabinets.
It was me, cooking the eggs and toast.
Thank you for that. And thank you for
bringing me back to life. Not in that order
at all. How did you sleep?
The Pie-Maker had grown accustomed to the
sound of her breathing, the smell of her skin
and the feeling his heart made when it looked
out his eyes and saw her sleeping in the next
bed. He had not--
Slept great.
Are you sure? ‘Cause that smile wouldn’t
vibrate anything off anything.
As he forces a bigger smile...
The Pie-Maker wondered if moving a little bit
apart hadn’t moved them a little bit apart.
They smile at each other, not sure what to do next...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
A little bit to the West...
PUSH IN ON EMERSON as he holds a cigar, phone to his ear as all
the lines blink:
(pushing phone buttons)
Emerson Cod, please hold. Emerson Cod, please
hold. Please hold.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED:
Well known for his uncanny ability to solve
murders and apprehend suspects, less so for his
silent partner who can wake the dead and ask
who did it, Emerson Cod’s business was booming.
He smiles at the busy phone, puffs and picks up his knitting,
about to take a call--
GEORGEANN (O.S.)
Mr. Cod?
GEORGEANN HEAPS, mid-40s, cool, well-kept and collected, has
entered...
GEORGEANN (CONT’D)
You the private investigator?
You know how to knock?
I did knock. I came in, said to myself, “I
hope this good man can help me. Knock-wood.”
And then I knocked.
(knocks)
My name is Georgeann Heaps.
It’s my nature to reward pushiness with
inattention, Ms. Heaps. If you want to make
an appointment--
For when? The tenth of never? I can see your
phone blinking like a casino sign.
(then)
I’m pushy, Mr. Cod, not an idiot. My teenage
daughter, Nikki, would disagree on that point
if she were here. But she’s not, because
she’s disappeared.
A missing persons case?
It’s been three weeks since I saw her last.
I’m desperate to find her.
(then)
Sorry, I’m not very good with emotion.
What emotion?
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED: (2)
All of them.
(then)
Police think my Nikki’s just another runaway,
so they won’t look for her. But that’s not who
she is. She’s always been sweet and helpful.
You ask her friends?
Even her best friend doesn’t know where she went,
and Nikki hates to be alone. A helping hand at
my side. Ever since she was a little girl.
She stops...
GEORGEANN (CONT’D)
I don’t mean to lose control like this.
Emerson watches her not lose control, then:
GEORGEANN (CONT’D)
Are you a parent or guardian, Emerson Cod?
Unprepared for the question, the answer tried
to hang onto the inside of his throat...
(mumbles)
Used to be.
Georgeann leans forward...
Did you say, “Used to be”?
I said I’ll take the case.
The words that choked in Emerson Cod’s throat were
that he, too, was the parent of a missing daughter.
And she and Nikki Heaps were not the only missing
persons that morning. There was another...

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - FLASHBACK (SHOT IN EPISODE 201)

lines.text: Olive has a meltdown...
After falling apart in what had come to be
called a “world-class tanty”...
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 7.

scenes.heading: INT. OLIVE’S APARTMENT - FLASHBACK (SHOT IN EPISODE 201)

lines.text: Her STEAMER TRUNKS stacked up.
...Olive Snook had packed all her worldly
belongings and moved out of her apartment in
the middle of the night.

scenes.heading: EXT. PIE HOLE - NIGHT - FLASHBACK (SHOT IN EPISODE 201)

lines.text: Lily and Olive drive away in the station wagon...
And Aunt Lily, panicked that Olive, in her
delicate state, might let slip some very big
secrets, whisked Olive off to a nunnery in
the country.

scenes.heading: INT. NUNNERY - OLIVE SNOOK’S ROOM - DAY

lines.text: OLIVE, in a nun’s habit, sits on her bed.
But not even Olive’s new austere daily life of
pretending to be a nun-in-training and
pretending to be austere, could keep those
secrets from spilling forth.
She’s talking to someone, O.S.--
So, Chuck’s mother isn’t some woman who died
in childbirth. In fact, she’s not dead at
all. Dying maybe, from all the drinking. But
alive and pretending to be her Aunt Lily.
REVEAL she is unburdening to PIGBY, who listens--
OLIVE (CONT’D)
And Lily doesn’t ever want her sister, Vivian,
to find this out because Vivian was engaged to
Chuck’s father when she got pregnant. And he
admitted to having an affair, but told Vivian
it was with someone else. So Vivian called it
off. And Lily came here to have baby Chuck in
secret-- Are you even listening to me?
ON PIGBY, blankly piglike. Oink.
Pigby enjoyed the warbling sounds that the
nice-smelling thing-that-fed-him made.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED:
Oh, Pigby, at least here, these secrets can’t hurt
anybody else. And maybe this is my chance to get
away from all my troubles and start over. Maybe
it’s time to devote my life to a higher purpose.
MOTHER SUPERIOR steps into the doorway behind her...
Sister Olive, it’s time for middle-mid-morning
prayers in the chapel.
Olive sighs, rolls her eyes and makes a “bluchhh” face to Pigby,
then turns with a bright smile--
Coming, Mother Superior.
As Olive leaves...
As Olive set off to make the best of her new
life, she was sorely missed in the one she
left behind...
Bustling.
The Pie Hole buzzes with CUSTOMERS. Chuck refills coffee at the
booths. Ned, in his apron, turns ’round to look at the door
every time the BELLS JINGLE.
The service here is terrible.
There is no service. Service left in the
middle of the night. Chuck’s just filling in.
Chuck sits, pooped.
When is Employee of the Mouth coming back?
Don’t know.
(to Emerson)
You pretend you don’t miss Olive, but you do.
And I do, too. I wish I knew where she went.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED:
Ned turns to watch the door again--
(to Ned)
Would you please quit looking at the door?
Every time I hear the bells, I think Chuck’s
aunts are gonna walk in again.
I took care of Lily and Vivian for 20 years
and they never left the house. What happened
was incredibly unusual.
Please take this the right way, but so is
being dead-but-not-dead.
Amen.
And while I might be shocked and amazed to see
your aunts walk in here again, people who are
dead-but-not-dead traditionally come up against
angry mobs with pitchforks and torches.
Chuck puts on her sunglasses, adjusts her kerchief...
This better?
(then)
You didn’t sleep well.
It was deep and perfect, like a nap in the
backseat of a car after a day at the beach.
Does anybody want to make any money?
He breaks the tension, opens a case folder--
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Sweet Nikki Heaps -- disappeared three weeks
ago. Mother says she’s a good girl, helpful
and selfless -- not the kind of person you’d
expect to run off. Thinks maybe she was
tricked, abducted or cajoled away.
Ned flips to an 8x10 PICTURE of Nikki, an awkward, frizzy-
haired, pimply-faced teenage girl. Chuck points to another girl
in the picture, RANDI JEAN.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED: (2)
Who’s that behind her?
Randi Jean, her best friend. I already spoke
with her and she doesn’t know anything.
Lemme talk to Randi.
(then)
She’s not going to tell a big P.I. the truth
and rat out her friend.
SOME NIFTY TIME TRANSITION TO:
A rebellious teenager, RANDI JEAN, 16, sits opposite Chuck.
I’m not gonna tell you anything about Nikki,
okay? I’ve made up my mind. And you should
know my dad says my mind is like an old
refrigerator in a deserted lot. If a secret’s
out there playing around and it climbs in -- it
ain’t never getting out, okay? So quit asking.
As Chuck opens the folder...
Emerson and Ned face away, sitting side-by-side at the counter.
Emerson reads a folded paper next to his plate of pie.
That girl’s not gonna tell her anything.
We’re gonna need some new leads, fast.
Maybe the client’s got more to tell.
It sounds silly when you say, “The client.”
Lingo doesn’t suit you.
I’m just saying, maybe Nikki’s mother’s hiding
something. People don’t run away for no reason.
Sure they do.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED:
You don’t think it’s curious that Olive left
in the middle of the night? Because I’m
curious. I’m very curious.
(still reading)
“Curious” is tighty-whitey for “angry.” And
you’re not angry ‘cause Olive left. You’re
angry ‘cause Olive left and Dead Girl moved
her ass into the empty apartment.
You’re wrong.
Person gets a little sip of a fresh start,
they want to drink it from the hose. Today,
an apartment across the hall; tomorrow, Paris
and a croissant-maker named Phillipe.
That’s not who Chuck is.
A mistake, you did make.
Yoda, you are not.
Chuck arrives as Randi Jean leaves in the b.g...
Nikki’s living with her boyfriend in his van
out on Airport Road. His name’s Rocky.
How’d you do it?
The dead girl had improvised...
POP TO:

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - BOOTH - FLASHBACK - MOMENTS BEFORE

lines.text: As they eat pie...
Nikki’s mother is worried.
Hello. That was kind of the point. Maybe her
mom won’t be such a Medicated Pad next time
Nikki wants to go out on a weeknight.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 12.
CONTINUED:
Where did she get the guts to run away from home?
You think it took guts? Most people just
think it was stupid.
I just moved out on my own and that’s scary.
Are you trying to find things in common so
I’ll lower my guard and tell you where Nikki
is? ‘Cause the “good cop” thing won’t work.
I know. I hate when people do that “good cop”
thing to me, too.
Really?
Sometimes it makes me so mad I want to run
away. Like Nikki.
That’s not why she ran away. She wants to be
a big star, but her mom wouldn’t take her
seriously. Nikki’s over being “Sweet Little
Nikki,” but her mom can’t see.
(catches herself)
Shoot. I didn’t want to tell you that.
I didn’t want you to tell me either! Isn’t
that weird?
We are so alike.
If we ran away together, do you think we’d end
up where Nikki is?
I wish. She moved in with a cute guy in a
really tricked-out van. He’s in entertainment.
Oh my gosh! That guy with the crazy van with the
thing who does that entertainment. I know him!
You know Rocky Boselli?
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 13.
CONTINUED: (2)
Chuck smiles...
RANDI JEAN (CONT’D)
Shoot.
A big VAN by the side of the road. Ned knocks on the back--
Nikki Heaps? Are you in there? Hello?
There’s no answer. As Emerson opens the door, Chuck notices the
sticker -- “Mimes do it with IMAGINATION.”
“Mimes do it with imagination.” That’s cute.
Emerson’s looking in. Ned recoils from the smell.
Thing should have said, “If the van’s a-
rockin’, I’m being murdered.”
ROCKY BOSELLI, a mime in mime clothes, lies on the bed, a
trickle of blood at the corner of his mouth. Chuck, Ned and
Emerson, wearing kerchiefs over their mouths and noses, lean
over.
Looks like he’s been dead for about a week.
(starts his watch)
Ready? One minute...
He TOUCHES Rocky, who opens his eyes and smiles, sitting up.
Are you Rocky?
Rocky nods and smiles. He’s not speaking.
He really is a mime.
(to Rocky)
Hi, sweetie.
Were you living with Nikki Heaps?
Rocky nods with a bittersweet smile, mimes taking out his own
heart and breaking it in two.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 14.
CONTINUED:
CHUCK (O.S.)
She broke your heart?
Did she kill you?
He shrugs (doesn’t know). Then, he begins to mime the story: He
woke up (stretch, yawn), then was putting on his makeup when he
started choking--
Okay. That’s enough.
Emerson points his gun. The mime instantly begins to speak--
I think someone poisoned my makeup. I don’t
know who.
Where’s Nikki now?
She’s with some clown.
A moment... Does he really mean...
A real clown?
(”What else would it be?”)
Yeah.
(then)
We met the jackass and all his jackass buddies
at the disco. They were with the traveling
circus. This one dude was telling her all
these stories about their big, glamorous life
on the road. Next day, she took off.
“Took off”?
Yeah. Said she wanted a fresh start. That
was the last I saw of her.
Ned and Emerson exchange a look...
I’m so sorry, Rocky.
This circus got a name?
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT ONE 15.
CONTINUED: (2)
“A Circus of Fun.” I know, it sucks. They
can’t have gotten that far.
(then)
Hey, if you find Nikki, would you mind giving
her this poem? She’s a sweet girl.
Rocky hands Chuck a poem, written on the back of a flyer.
Sure. Would you mind doing the “glass box”?
I love that.
Rocky starts to mime the walls around him. Ned RE-DEADS him and
he slumps back down.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
Hey.
(to Ned)
Thank you.
(then)
Looks like we gotta go to the circus.
Off a big top music STING--
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT TWO 16.
FADE IN:
Chuck, in disguise, works the counter.
CUSTOMER #1
Can I see a menu, please?
Sure. You can see one right over there. In
the pile of menus.
CUSTOMER #1
What’s with the attitude, lady?
What was with the attitude, lady, was this:
Emerson waits by the front door in the b.g. Chuck and Ned talk
as CUSTOMERS enter and exit...
What do you mean, I can’t come?
Someone’s got to run the Pie Hole with Olive
gone.
How about the Pie-Maker?
Emerson needs me.
Why? There’s no dead body to wake up.
(re: nearby patrons)
Nice. Anyone not hear that?
Are you upset with me? Is this about
something else?
This was about something else.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED:
Nothing else. I promise I’ll let you come
next time.
Thanks for your permission.
You don’t need my permission.
Thanks for your permission not to need your
permission.
It’s a traveling circus. Not a wait-around-
for-you-to-work-your-junk-out circus.
I’ll be back soon.
I’ll be here forever.
She walks back toward the kitchen. Ned watches.
That was curious.
Emerson starts out, Ned hesitates before following...
As the Pie-Maker wondered if Chuck moving out
was making him passive or aggressive or both...
Olive sits in a shaft of sunlight, a contemplative smile.
...Olive wondered when her new beginning would
feel like it had begun.
That’s it.
(a cleansing breath)
I am now more bored than I have ever been before.
Mother Superior leans in--
It’s time for late-mid-afternoon prayers,
Sister Olive.
Olive turns before Mother Superior can leave--
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED:
Excuse me, Mother Superior. Does something
ever happen where you think everything is
kind of blah -- like blah brick walls, blah
faux-Shaker furniture, blah Good Works and
then, Shazam! All the little boring stuff is
suddenly full of meaning?
Like an epiphany?
Bingo.
Not very often. It takes time to fill a life
with meaning. Our days here are not easy,
Sister Olive, but you will find that with hard
work and personal sacrifice, you will strip away
everything from your old life and start anew.
(forced excitement)
Grr--ate!
Come along soon. Don’t be late.
Mother Superior exits, passing another SISTER who hides her face
as she enters. Olive barely notices, sighs...
You want a chapel-buddy, Sister?
The nun lowers her habit -- it’s LILY.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
(hushed)
Lily? I thought you went home. When did you
come back?
(leaving again)
I can’t be seen. Meet me in the chapel tonight.
When?
Early mid-middle-night prayer.
And Lily’s off again...
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT TWO 19.
A big balloon archway that marks the entrance to the small,
traveling circus -- think FELLINI. A big tent (big enough for
one ring), and a small midway with a ticket booth, several game
stands and a trailer office.
Ned and Emerson get out of Emerson’s car...
(looking around)
This ain’t a circus. A circus should smell
like popcorn and cotton candy. Not wet
sawdust and underarm. This is a freak show.
Ned and Emerson start to walk, passing SEVERAL JUGGLERS in
MASKS, A BEARDED LADY and a TATTOO-COVERED MAN...
Why would sweet Nikki Heaps run away here?
They have come to the OFFICE TRAILER, flanked on either side by
an AERIALIST REHEARSAL SCAFFOLD. SEVERAL costumed AERIALISTS
practice in the b.g.
People decide to leave and start over, a switch
flips, a fuse blows and everything’s gotta
change. You can’t have half a revolution.
(off Ned)
And don’t look at me with those psychobabbly
eyes, like this case is personal to me.
No eyes. Just looking.
(then)
If you want to talk--
As Emerson turns to respond to Ned, there is a WHOOSHING sound.
PIERRE, a French-Canadian acrobat in costume, holding a
cigarette, drops down in front of them, upside-down. Emerson
and Ned YELL, surprised...
You’re not allowed back here. We don’t allow
any stubs snooping around.
“Stubs”?
There are two kinds of people in the world.
Those that take risks and make you feel
something besides the dull thudding of your
own heart. And those that pay to watch.
(MORE)
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT TWO 20.
CONTINUED:
(maybe he needs more...)
With a ticket stub in their pock--
I got it.
We’re investigating the disappearance of a
young girl and the murder of her boyfriend.
(shrugs)
Sorry. I can’t help you.
You ever seen the separate police lockup for
cocky acrobats? ‘Cause I haven’t.
I am upside-down, my friend. Not foolish.
The girl was last seen with the clowns.
Talk to Mr. Arno in the office trailer. He’s
in charge of the Circus of Fun.
Thank you.
But you should know, there’s two things clowns
make around here: Balloon animals, and enemies.
With that, he ascends back UP, OUT OF FRAME. Ned and Emerson
proceed up the stairs to--
Emerson and Ned sit across from ARNO, 50s, gruff circus lifer,
looking at the open case folder and the picture of Nikki...
I don’t know her, but we got lots of people
passing through. Hard to keep track of
everybody.
The girl we’re looking for was hitching a ride
with a mime who ended up dead.
Guess that’s one box he won’t get out of.
PUSHING DAISIES #202 "Circus Circus" 08/07/08 FINAL VERSION ACT TWO 21.
CONTINUED:
Arno’s Kathy Lee-esque ASSISTANT SNORT-GIGGLES from her desk in
the corner.
ARNO (CONT’D)
The clowns haze the newbies pretty bad. If
she didn’t quit, she was probably assigned to
apprentice one of ‘em.
Where can we find these clowns?
Drunk in a ditch would be my guess. They
usually stumble in just before showtime. And
they always travel in a pack.
Like wolves?
More like cigarettes.
More SNORT-GIGGLES from his assistant.
Thanks for your help.
I’m sorry I don’t remember the girl.
Another SNORT-GIGGLE, and we--

scenes.heading: EXT. ARNO’S OFFICE TRAILER - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: Did you notice his secretary snort-giggled
whenever he made a joke?
Yeah, but then she also snort-giggled--
--when he said he didn’t remember her. ‘Could
have been a nervous snort-giggle--
‘Cause she knew he was lying. She’s worth a
second look.

Said everyone thought she was a wallflower, so

And in return, you were gonna put her in

She said she’d do anything not to go back to

A distant BOOM. From outside.

Emerson turns to the window--

The HELMETED LITTLE MAN crashes through THE WALL, SMASHING INTO
